findings.title: Required verification contract is not green or bound to the current specification
findings.description: T-001.contract.json marks the required regression and placeholder-scan checks false, explicitly states that the full regression run did not complete, and retains a stale spec_revision instead of the current digest. Therefore the supplied verification contract cannot establish acceptance against the implementation and specification under review.
findings.required_fix: Run the complete required checks, resolve or formally obtain the required human acceptance for placeholder findings, and issue a fresh independently generated contract bound to the current specification revision.

findings.title: No current independent security review covers the shipped runner
findings.description: The security review covers a deleted draft without a recorded digest. Its addendum identifies substantive subsequent changes to the shipped runner and explicitly says it does not reissue PASS. This violates T-001's security-review Done When for a high-risk, security-sensitive protected-file publisher.
findings.required_fix: Perform and record a fresh independent security review against the exact current runner bytes, including the changed payload set, portable mode handling, failure classification, and partial-publication reporting.

findings.title: The Windows secure-publish implementation remains unexecuted
findings.description: The runner contains a separate Windows implementation using NtCreateFile, NtSetInformationFile, handle-relative rename, and reparse-point checks, but the evidence states that this path was only reviewed statically and has never executed. The two reported green entry points invoke the same PowerShell suite on the macOS host, so they do not verify this security-sensitive platform branch.
findings.required_fix: Execute the contract and security regression suite on Windows against the current runner and retain evidence that exercises the Windows publisher, rename, reparse-point rejection, corruption detection, and partial-failure reporting paths.
